query: How does Postgres assign a WAL LSN and reserve space in the WAL buffers when inserting a new WAL record?

matches.reason: Top-level WAL insertion routine that reserves space, fills in xl_prev/CRC, copies the record into WAL buffers, and returns the end LSN, implementing the documented two-step reserve-then-copy protocol.

The spinlock-protected core that atomically advances Insert->CurrBytePos to reserve exactly 'size' bytes of WAL and converts the byte position into the actual XLogRecPtr (LSN) for StartPos/EndPos/xl_prev.
Maps a reserved WAL location to its slot in the shared WAL buffer cache, initializing a new buffer page via AdvanceXLInsertBuffer if the space isn't yet backed by an in-memory page.
